intended_object: A combinatorial (PL) n-manifold, possibly with boundary: a simplicial complex in which the link of every vertex is a combinatorial (n−1)-sphere or a combinatorial (n−1)-ball, i.e. a complex PL-equivalent (stellar equivalent) to ∂Δⁿ or Δⁿ⁻¹ (Rourke–Sanderson, Lickorish). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body has two cases. For n+1, every vertex {v} ∈ K must have `link K {v}` be a combinatorial n-sphere or a combinatorial n-ball. These are defined as being stellar equivalent, up to an injective relabeling of vertices, to `simplexBoundary V` with |V| = n+2 or to `simplex V` with |V| = n+1. This is the standard Lickorish / Rourke–Sanderson vertex-link definition. By Newman/Alexander, stellar equivalence agrees with PL equivalence for finite complexes. Relabeling into `ι ⊕ ℕ` means a small vertex type never runs out of fresh vertices for the moves.

The link is defined as {ρ nonempty | ρ disjoint from σ, ρ ∪ σ ∈ K}, the usual link with the empty face left out. So in dimension 0 the textbook condition "every vertex link is the (−1)-sphere, i.e. empty" becomes `link K {v} = ⊥`, which is exactly the 0 case of the definition. Matching on n instead of using truncated subtraction avoids a wrong 0-dimensional case.

Using only vertex links (not links of all simplices) is the usual formulation, and it is equivalent because links of simplices sit inside vertex links. The definition does not require K to be finite. This matches the general notion, since only the vertex links (closed stars) have to be finite, and the library proves that they are.

The setting is a general vertex type `ι` with decidable equality, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no notion of combinatorial or PL manifold for abstract simplicial complexes.
